title: Original Jurisdiction reports on traditionally defense-focused Big Law firms entering plaintiff-side litigation
summary: David Lat, author of Original Jurisdiction, reports that traditionally defense-focused Big Law firms are increasingly representing corporate clients as plaintiffs. Driven by client demand and supported by legal finance, firms are taking on high-value affirmative matters using more flexible fee structures, allowing them to compete for plaintiff-side work while managing risk and preserving their core economic model. The article features perspectives from Burford’s Evan Meyerson and Vanessa Biondo. Learn more.
body_markdown:
David Lat, author of Original Jurisdiction, reports that traditionally defense-focused Big Law firms are increasingly representing corporate clients as plaintiffs. Driven by client demand and supported by legal finance, firms are taking on high-value affirmative matters using more flexible fee structures, allowing them to compete for plaintiff-side work while managing risk and preserving their core economic model. The article features perspectives from Burford’s[Evan Meyerson](https://www.burfordcapital.com/about-us/our-team/evan-meyerson/) and[Vanessa Biondo](https://www.burfordcapital.com/about-us/our-team/vanessa-biondo/) .


Read the full article[here](https://davidlat.substack.com/p/defense-focused-biglaw-moves-into-plaintiff-side-work-affirmative-litigation) .
